thread:
Alex: heads up — seeing a few pods bounce between gpu nodegroup and cpu nodes in us-west-2. pods with the old toleration key are Pending, cluster-autoscaler scaled down some GPU nodes earlier :grimacing:
Jamal: ugh. any logs from the scheduler?
Alex: checked `kubectl get pods -o wide` — Pending with `0/0 nodes available` and `node(s) had taint {nvidia.com/gpu: NoSchedule}`
Priya: can you paste the pod tolerations? maybe key name mismatch after the nodepool rename we did last week
Alex: here: ```yaml
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Seán: ah yeah we switched to the cloud provider taint `nvidia.com/gpu` during the pool migration. pods still tolerating `gpu` won't match.
Lucy: infra-bot just posted a scale-down event around 1852504200 that removed 3 spot gpu nodes. maybe the autoscaler thought they were idle.
infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scaledDownNodeGroup: ng-gpu-spot-usw2 count:3 reason: underutilized
Marta: do we have fallback routing? some services have `nodeAffinity` set incorrectly and are landing on cpu nodes which causes CUDA lib load failures at runtime.
Alex: exact error from the failed job: `Failed to allocate device: no devices found` -> app expects GPUs but ended up on cpu nodes.
Jamal: quick triage: 1) update tolerations to `nvidia.com/gpu` 2) add preferredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity for gpu label 3) set podPriority/Preemption to avoid autoscaler killing gpu nodes while pods boot
Priya: we need a short-term quarantine: add a mutating webhook? or patch deployment to include both toleration keys so older images still schedule.
Alex: patched a canary: added both keys in tolerations and a `nodeAffinity` preference to `kubernetes.io/role=gpu` label. rolling restart in progress.
Seán: good. for the longer term we should standardize on one taint key and add a validation job in CI to catch mismatches when nodepool names/labels change.
Lucy: cost note — if we stop draining spot gpu nodes aggressively, we pay more but avoid these warm-up failures. tradeoff: roughly $0.9/hr per p3 spot (est).
Marta: also noticed autoscaler config uses low `scaleDownUtilizationThreshold`. we can raise it for gpu nodegroups so they don't scale down during short idle windows.
Jamal: also consider `--balance-similar-node-groups` flag and `max-empty-bulk-delete=0` to slow down deletes.
Priya: added a quick script to scan all Deployments for tolerations not matching current taints. running now, will post results.
Alex: output snippet from the script: ```
deployments-found: 6
mismatches:
 - model-server-v2: toleration key: gpu
 - batch-renderer: toleration key: legacy-gpu
```
Seán: sweet. can we push a small rollout: patch the 6 to include `nvidia.com/gpu` toleration OR change to `operator: Exists` to be more resilient?
Marta: `Exists` loses intent (any taint) — i'd prefer explicit keys for audit. but for a short window `Exists` might be ok.
Lucy: FYI we have a scheduled scaling policy at midnight that reduces gpu pool to min=2. maybe combine with time-based scale prevention for deploy windows.
Jamal: action items: (1) patch 6 deployments canary -> both tolerations (2) change autoscaler config for gpu group to be less aggressive (3) CI check for taint/toleration drift (4) doc a rollback plan if nodes run out of GPUs
Alex: I'm on (1) and will monitor. Priya take (3)?
Priya: taking (3). will open PR for a k8s lint check and add it to pre-merge jobs.
Alex: thanks. infra-bot — keep us posted on any additional scale events.
infra-bot: alert: new scaleDownAttempt on ng-gpu-spot-usw2 at 1852504600 - prevented by activity: pending pods detected
Seán: nice - looks like the canary made the scheduler detect activity.
Lucy: follow-up: let's schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to decide default taint key and autoscaler thresholds. :calendar:
Marta: agreed. I'll draft an RFC with cost/availability tradeoffs.
Alex: closing the thread for now — canary healthy, 2 pods scheduled onto gpu nodes. will reopen if anything else pops. :thumbsup:
